properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, asking whether CAP/PACELC applies to reflow2's own design. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

⭐ THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH KEEPING: reflow2 HAS ALREADY MADE THESE TRADE-OFFS, REPEATEDLY AND DELIBERATELY, AND HAS NEVER NAMED THEM AS ONE CLASS. Checked against the graph rather than asserted:

THE STORE IS CP. One RocksDB store, single-writer by construction. A second writer is refused rather than served — `cap:degraded-surface` exists precisely to explain that refusal, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` settled what a locked-out seat gets: "a read-only view as of open, not a catchable-up secondary". That is textbook CP with a stale-read escape hatch. `cap:stale-seat-refusal` and `req:stale-seat-knows` are the write half: refuse rather than clobber.

THE RECORD IS AP. `docs/design/reflow2.json` travels by git. Everyone works offline, diverges freely, reconciles later — `cap:merge-designs`, `cap:git-merge-driver`, `cap:portability`, three-way merge with rerere. Nobody blocks. `cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` and `sync_status` are, precisely, an eventual-consistency staleness detector: they tell a seat the shared record moved ahead of it and name what arrived.

AND `dec:advisory-concurrency` IS AN EXPLICIT AP CHOICE WITH EMPIRICAL BACKING. Its words: "seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, NEVER BY EXCLUSION… when two claims cross, the winner is whichever landed first in git history, and both parties can verify that independently." It names what it rejected — "a coordination service or lock manager" — and why: "a lock is exactly what took FIVE OF SIX SESSIONS OFFLINE on 2026-07-25." That is choosing A over C after measuring the cost of C, which is the CAP decision made properly and never called by its name.

⇒ SO THE CANDIDATE READING IS: reflow2 is PC/EC in the store and PA/EL in the record. In normal operation it does not block on syncing the record — you work locally and export later, which is choosing L. PACELC's actual contribution here is that second half: the store-versus-record tension is NOT rare-failure behaviour, it is what every ordinary session does all day.

🛑 AND THE SHARP PART, WHICH IS WHY THIS MIGHT BE MORE THAN A RELABELLING: THE SEAM BETWEEN THE CP STORE AND THE AP RECORD IS WHERE AN UNUSUAL SHARE OF THIS PROJECT'S BUGS HAVE LIVED. Not a claim about all bugs — a pattern worth testing:
  · "the design graph does NOT branch with git" — one store serves every branch, so an export carries another branch's writes. Caught once as four phantom drifts that would have merged cleanly.
  · The whole export procedure — restore from origin/main, export exactly once, verify prev_content_hash — is a HAND-OPERATED RECONCILIATION PROTOCOL between the two models, and every one of its documented traps is a reconciliation bug.
  · The mirror-refresh defect (v0.12.0 → v0.29.0): a stale pin reporting FRESH after a failed refresh is a staleness-register lie, which is the classic AP failure mode.
  · 2026-08-12, this session: creating nodes after exporting silently put the record behind the graph. Nothing prevented it; only a later `compare_designs` would have caught it.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. Record the observation and stop. CHEAP, and possibly correct: nothing would compute differently, and the choices are already made, individually, with better-reasoned rationales than "CAP says so."

B — USE IT AS A LENS ONLY, in prose. Name the store/record split in AGENTS.md so a newcomer meets it once instead of rediscovering it through the export traps. Cheap, no code, no schema.

C — MAKE THE SEAM A FIRST-CLASS THING THE GRAPH KNOWS. If the record and the store are two replicas with a hand-run reconciliation protocol, then the protocol deserves to be modelled — the traps are currently memory and prose, not structure. Most expensive, and the one where something could actually compute.

D — TREAT IT AS A REQUIREMENTS SOURCE. Ask what reflow2's own availability target IS. It has never been stated, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` answered a CAP question without one.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. CAP IS ABOUT REPLICATED DATA UNDER NETWORK PARTITION, and reflow2's "partition" is mostly a HUMAN and PROCESS boundary — git branches, separate sessions, a person on a plane. Borrowing a theorem outside its domain is how architectures acquire vocabulary they cannot cash. The single strongest objection.

⚠️ 2. THERE IS NO REPLICATION PROTOCOL HERE. CAP's interesting cases begin with replicas that must agree. reflow2 has one writer per store and delegates the distributed half wholesale to git — so "reflow2 is AP" may be a statement about GIT, correctly, and nothing about reflow2.

⚠️ 3. THE CHOICES ARE ALREADY MADE AND ALREADY BETTER-ARGUED. `dec:advisory-concurrency` rests on a measured outage of five of six sessions. Relabelling that as "we chose AP" is strictly less information than what is recorded.

⚠️ 4. NOTHING WOULD COMPUTE DIFFERENTLY under A or B, and this project's own bar — `dec:exploratory-staging`, the ility work — is whether a distinction changes a computation.

📌 A FAIR POINT FOR THE IDEA: the export traps keep being rediscovered, session after session, and live in a memory note rather than in the design. If naming the seam is what makes them explicable rather than a list of superstitions, that is worth something even under option B.
properties.name: OPEN — is reflow2 already a CP store behind an AP record, and is that seam where its recurring bugs live?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept because the descriptive half is verifiable today against existing nodes — dec:advisory-concurrency, dec:read-while-held-mechanism, cap:stale-seat-refusal, cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced — and because it offers a single explanation for a family of recurring export and staleness bugs that are currently carried as procedure rather than as design. The counter-arguments are recorded beside rather than against; the strongest is that reflow2 delegates the distributed problem to git, which would make this a statement about git.
